finding.claim: Result caching only records a token's exp/nbf window when the payload has a numeric iat. A token with exp (and/or nbf) but no iat is cached with min=0 and max=now+tolerance+cacheTTL (default 600000 ms). It keeps being accepted from the cache after its exp passes, for up to cacheTTL after it was first cached. This is an authentication/expiry bypass when caching is enabled.
finding.source: A signed JWT that carries exp (or nbf) but no iat claim, sent repeatedly to a verifier created with the cache option. The attacker is a holder of an expired or soon-to-expire token, or the token is a legitimately issued one whose lifetime the app expects to be enforced.
finding.sink: verify() cache-hit branch at src/verifier.js:364-378 returns the cached payload without re-running verifyToken's exp/nbf validators.

trace.note: First successful verification calls cacheSet with the payload
hasIat is false when payload.iat is not a number
The whole block that sets cacheValue[1] (nbf) and cacheValue[2] (exp / iat+maxAge) is skipped, so both stay 0
cacheValue[2] === 0, so it is set to maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL (default 10 min), ignoring the token's own exp
A later call with the same token reads the cache entry
now <= max passes even though now > exp*1000, so the cache hit is returned (line 377)

finding.guards_checked: The decoder and verifyToken exp/nbf validators (src/verifier.js:304-323) are enforced on a cache miss, but the cache-hit path at 364-378 skips them. cacheTTL is validated as a finite number >= 0 but defaults to 600000 ms. Neither requiredClaims nor iat is enforced by default. errorCacheTTL only affects cached errors. The cache is disabled by default, so this applies only when cache is set.
